theme: Ureteric bud and nephric duct morphogenesis in kidney development
story: The centre is the formation, elongation and branching of the ureteric bud from the nephric duct, the epithelial tube that gives rise to the ureter and the collecting system of the metanephric kidney. Regulatory terms (positive regulation of epithelial tube formation, regulation of mesonephros and metanephros development, negative regulation of kidney development, regulation of kidney size) describe the controls that set how much the bud grows and branches. Together the cluster covers how the urinary drainage tree is built and how its extent determines final kidney size.

theme: Inhibitory receptor control of phagocyte and antibody responses
story: The centre is inhibitory immunoreceptor signalling, exemplified by SIRP family interactions (the CD47-SIRPalpha 'don't eat me' signal) and Fc receptor inhibitory signalling via ITIM-bearing receptors such as FcgammaRIIB. These brakes explain the negative regulation of phagocytosis, neutrophil activation and B cell receptor signalling, while positive regulation of Fc receptor stimulatory signalling and of immunoglobulin-mediated humoral responses represent the activating side they counterbalance. The cluster as a whole is about tuning antibody- and Fc receptor-driven effector responses by balancing activating and inhibitory receptors on myeloid and B cells.

theme: Base excision repair, alkylation reversal and active DNA demethylation
story: The centre is base excision repair: DNA glycosylases recognise and excise damaged purines and pyrimidines, leaving AP sites that are resolved through single-nucleotide replacement and single-strand break repair, including NEIL1/NEIL3 defects and NEIL3-mediated interstrand cross-link unhooking. Direct reversal of alkylation damage by MGMT, ALKBH2 and ALKBH3 sits alongside as an alternative repair route for alkylated bases. The same glycosylase machinery is reused in active DNA demethylation, where TET enzymes oxidise 5-methylcytosine and TDG excises the products, linking repair to CpG island demethylation and gene activation.

theme: RAS-MAPK pathway negative regulation and oncogenic mutant signalling
story: The centre is the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade viewed through its off-switches: RAS GAPs (including NF1), negative feedback from ERK, ERK inactivation by dual-specificity phosphatases (the threonine and tyrosine dephosphorylation terms) and general negative regulation of Ras and ERK signalling. Disease-associated mutants in RAS, RAS GAPs, MRAS, MAP2K and MAPK show what happens when these brakes are lost or bypassed, and RSK activation is the downstream ERK output that also participates in feedback. The cluster describes how MAPK signal amplitude is limited and how mutations in RASopathies and cancer escape that limitation.

theme: Oncogenic RAF/BRAF signalling and MAPK cascade feedback control
story: The centre is RAF activation and its oncogenic variants: high-, moderate- and kinase-dead BRAF mutants (including paradoxical activation), BRAF/RAF1 fusions, RAF1 mutants and MRAS-SHOC2 complexes that drive RAF, feeding MEK and ERK activation. Downstream mutants in RAS, MAP2K and MAPK and NF1 loss extend the picture along the cascade, while ERK inactivation by phosphatases, negative feedback, and negative regulation of Ras/ERK signalling form the counterbalancing brakes. Together the cluster depicts the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK axis as a module whose output is set by RAF dimer activation and phosphatase/feedback restraint, and how cancer and RASopathy mutations dysregulate it.

theme: Immediate-early growth factor and stress transcriptional response via AP-1
story: The centre is the immediate-early gene response: AP-1 (FOS/JUN) activation and network, NR4A nuclear receptor genes induced by growth factors, and p38 MAPK signalling that triggers them in response to external stimuli. TNF-alpha/NF-kB and PI3K-AKT-mTOR hallmark sets represent the parallel signalling inputs that co-induce these genes, while cell cycle and growth arrest reflects one outcome of the response. The cluster as a whole captures the rapid transcriptional programme a cell mounts on receiving mitogenic, inflammatory or stress stimuli.

theme: Intraflagellar transport and protein trafficking into cilia
story: The centre is intraflagellar transport, the anterograde and retrograde motor-driven movement along the axoneme that builds and maintains the cilium. Cargo-targeting routes (BBSome, VxPx motif, ARL13B-driven INPP5E delivery, myristoylated-protein trafficking, receptor localisation to non-motile cilia) explain how specific membrane and signalling proteins are delivered into the ciliary compartment. Cilium assembly and beat frequency regulation round out the picture: the cluster is about constructing cilia and stocking them with the right proteins for sensing and motility.

theme: Nephron formation from metanephric mesenchyme during kidney development
story: The centre is nephrogenesis: metanephric mesenchyme cells are maintained, undergo mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition to form the renal vesicle, then progress through comma- and S-shaped bodies to differentiated nephron tubules with proximal/distal patterning. Earlier steps (intermediate mesoderm, pronephros, nephric duct formation, ureteric bud elongation) provide the developmental origin and the inductive bud that triggers nephron formation. The cluster describes how the functional units of the kidney arise from embryonic mesoderm.

theme: Transition metal ion transport, homeostasis and detoxification
story: The centre is uptake, distribution and storage of essential trace metals: iron (transferrin cycling, ferroportin, DMT1, heme scavenging and assimilation), zinc (SLC39 import, SLC30 efflux, MTF1, metallothioneins), copper and manganese, with Mendelian disorders illustrating failures of each transporter. Responses to and detoxification of toxic metals (cadmium, mercury, lead, cobalt) use the same transporters and metallothionein/MTF1 sensing machinery, and glutathione transport and selenium responses contribute to buffering metal-induced oxidative stress. The cluster as a whole is about the cell's and body's metal economy: acquiring essential metals, keeping them at safe levels, and neutralising harmful ones.

theme: Receptor tyrosine kinase to RAS-ERK signalling and its regulation
story: The centre is RAS activation downstream of growth factor receptors (IGF1R-SHC, SOS, FGFR signalling modulated by FGFRL1 and Sprouty) leading through RAF to ERK1/ERK2 activation and AP-1 induction. Regulation by GAPs, phosphatase-mediated ERK inactivation, negative feedback and RASopathy/cancer mutants in RAS, NF1, MRAS-SHOC2, MAP2K and MAPK describe how signal strength is controlled and how it is corrupted. Side branches such as AKT inhibition of TSC and RIT/RIN signalling to p38 show related outputs; the cluster is the canonical growth factor-RAS-MAPK axis from receptor to nucleus.

theme: Glycerophospholipid synthesis, remodelling and membrane distribution
story: The centre is de novo synthesis of the major glycerophospholipids from CDP-diacylglycerol and the Kennedy pathway: PC, PE, PS, PG and cardiolipin, with acyl-chain remodelling of PG and cardiolipin. Transport and translocation terms (intermembrane lipid transfer, flippase-mediated aminophospholipid translocation, ANO6 calcium-activated scrambling) explain how these lipids are moved between organelles and across bilayer leaflets. Cardiolipin's link to mitochondrial fusion shows one functional endpoint; overall the cluster covers building membrane phospholipids and placing them where they are needed.

theme: p53-mediated DNA damage response: arrest, senescence, apoptosis
story: The centre is TP53 itself: its expression, phosphorylation, co-factor binding and degradation control, and its transcriptional programmes for G1 arrest (p21), DNA repair genes, death receptors and other apoptotic genes. Ionising radiation responses and DNA damage checkpoint signalling are the upstream triggers, while G2/M checkpoint elements (Cdc25A degradation, GTSE1, MASTL, CDK inhibition) are parallel or downstream cell cycle brakes. The cluster describes how DNA damage is converted, largely via p53, into cell cycle arrest, senescence or intrinsic apoptosis, and how p53 loss in cancer disables this.

theme: Chromosome segregation machinery in mitosis and meiosis
story: The centre is the shared machinery of cell division: chromosome condensation, sister chromatid cohesion establishment and resolution, centromere/CENP-A assembly, spindle assembly and checkpoint, Aurora A/PLK1 control, anaphase transition, nuclear envelope breakdown and reformation, and cytokinesis through midbody abscission. Meiosis-specific processes (DSB formation, synapsis, recombination, chiasma assembly, meiotic cohesion, female meiotic spindle and polar body extrusion) are the specialised variant of the same machinery. Proliferation signatures (mitotic spindle hallmark, MYC network, spermatogenesis) mark tissues where this programme runs; the cluster as a whole is about faithfully partitioning chromosomes into daughter cells or gametes.

theme: Notch receptor intracellular domain transcriptional signalling
story: The centre is canonical Notch signalling, in which the released Notch intracellular domain (here NOTCH3 and NOTCH4) enters the nucleus and activates HES/HEY-type target genes. Positive regulation of Notch target transcription and the hallmark Notch gene set describe the output, and negative regulation of the pathway describes its restraint. The cluster captures Notch-driven transcription as a cell-fate signalling module.

theme: GABA synthesis, vesicular loading and reuptake at synapses
story: The centre is the GABAergic transmitter cycle: GABA is synthesised from glutamate, loaded into acidified synaptic vesicles, released, and cleared by SLC6 reuptake transporters. Intracellular glutamate homeostasis supplies the precursor, and broader SLC-mediated neurotransmitter and organic ion/taurine-like (alkanesulfonate) transport reflect the transporter families involved. The cluster describes how inhibitory synapses produce, package and recycle their neurotransmitter.

theme: Endosomal TLR7/8/9 and cGAS-STING nucleic acid sensing
story: The centre is innate sensing of nucleic acids: endosomal TLR7, TLR8 and TLR9 detecting RNA and DNA, with SLC15A4-TASL driving IRF5 activation, and cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS-STING, including cGAMP import. TREX1 degradation of cytosolic DNA and the negative regulators prevent self nucleic acids from triggering the pathways, and defective TLR7 regulation by endogenous ligands illustrates autoimmune failure. The output is type I interferon (interferon-beta production and response); the cluster is about distinguishing foreign from self nucleic acid to launch antiviral interferon responses.

theme: Amino sugar, sialic acid and nucleotide-sugar biosynthesis for glycosylation
story: The centre is the hexosamine pathway: fructose-6-phosphate is converted by GFPT1 into glucosamine and on to UDP-N-acetylglucosamine, which feeds sialic acid synthesis (GNE, CMP-sialic acid) and N-linked glycosylation. Mannose metabolism, UDP-glucose and dolichyl-phosphate-glucose supply the other sugar donors, and N-acetylglucosamine/sialic acid catabolism represents their turnover. Disease terms (GFPT1 and ALG14 congenital myasthenic syndromes, GNE sialuria/myopathy) show the cluster's purpose: providing activated sugars for protein glycosylation, whose defects affect muscle and neuromuscular junctions.

theme: Type 2 immunity: Th2, IL-33 and eosinophil responses
story: The centre is the type 2 immune response: Th2 differentiation and production of IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13, triggered and amplified by the alarmin IL-33. Eosinophil activation, chemotaxis and migration and mast cell activation are the effector arms recruited by these cytokines. The response to nematodes shows the cluster's purpose: coordinating an anti-helminth (and allergic) immune programme.

theme: Nephron development from mesoderm to patterned tubules
story: The centre is nephrogenesis in the metanephric kidney: metanephric mesenchyme differentiates, forms renal vesicles, passes through comma- and S-shaped body stages, and becomes tubule epithelium with proximal/distal patterning. Intermediate mesoderm and pronephros formation give the developmental origin, and ureteric bud elongation provides the inductive partner. The cluster describes how nephrons, the kidney's filtering units, are built during embryogenesis.

theme: Early neural plate patterning and head/hindbrain regionalisation
story: The centre is anterior-posterior and dorsal-ventral patterning of the early neural plate: anterior and posterior neural plate formation, neural plate border specification, forebrain patterning, midbrain-hindbrain boundary and rhombomere development with anterior HOX activation. Neural crest fate commitment, neurocranium and adenohypophysis development and anterior head development describe the structures that arise from these patterned regions. The cluster is about how signalling-driven gene expression divides the embryonic nervous system and head into distinct territories.

theme: Dietary sugar absorption, glycogen metabolism and glucose homeostasis
story: The centre is glucose handling: intestinal digestion and absorption of hexoses, transport (SGLT1/2, GLUT2), phosphorylation by hexokinase/glucokinase, glycolysis and gluconeogenesis, and glycogen synthesis and breakdown. Fructose, galactose/lactose, glycerol, alditol and alanine metabolism feed into or out of the same hexose-phosphate pool. The many inborn errors (glycogen storage diseases, fructose intolerance, MODY2, Fanconi-Bickel, glucose-galactose malabsorption, Lafora disease) map failures of each step; the cluster as a whole describes how the body takes up, stores and releases carbohydrate to keep blood glucose stable.

theme: Chemokine-guided lymphocyte and dendritic cell trafficking to lymphoid organs
story: The centre is leukocyte homing: CCR7 and related chemokine receptors, S1P receptor signalling and integrin adhesion steer T cells, B cells, thymocytes and mature dendritic cells into and out of lymph nodes and the thymus. Cdc42 signalling, pseudopodium assembly and PLC/PKC signalling are the intracellular motility machinery, and lymph node development and marginal zone B cell differentiation reflect the tissues and cell fates shaped by this trafficking. The untitled module on integrin/growth-factor input to cytoskeleton fits as generic adhesion-migration signalling; overall the cluster is about bringing antigen-presenting cells and lymphocytes together in lymphoid tissue.

theme: Actin filament assembly, severing and crosslinking dynamics
story: The centre is the regulation of actin filament dynamics: polymerisation, Arp2/3 nucleation, barbed-end capping, severing and depolymerisation. Crosslinking and network formation organise filaments into structures such as ruffles that power actin-based cell motility. Caspase cleavage of cytoskeletal proteins represents dismantling of this network during apoptosis; the cluster as a whole is about building and remodelling the actin cytoskeleton.

theme: Deoxyribonucleotide and nucleoside catabolism and salvage
story: The centre is the breakdown of deoxyribonucleotides and deoxynucleosides: dUMP, dTMP, dCMP, dGMP and dAMP catabolism and pyrimidine degradation. Purine deoxynucleoside metabolism, with ADA and PNP deficiency, shows the clinically important arm in which failure to clear deoxyadenosine and deoxyguanosine poisons lymphocytes. Purine dNTP biosynthesis is the counterpart; the cluster is about maintaining a balanced deoxynucleotide pool by disposing of excess DNA precursors.

theme: Calcineurin-NFAT signalling in cardiac hypertrophy
story: The centre is calcineurin activation of NFAT, with its positive and negative regulation. In cardiomyocytes this pathway drives hypertrophic adaptation, explaining the terms for cardiac muscle adaptation, sarcomere organisation, cardiomyocyte growth and increased cell size. The cluster as a whole describes how calcium-calcineurin-NFAT signalling controls cardiac muscle growth in response to load.

theme: Thymic T cell selection, tolerance and thymocyte survival
story: The centre is thymocyte development: positive and negative selection, differentiation into CD8 and gamma-delta lineages, and Treg development under RUNX1 and FOXP3. Regulation of thymocyte proliferation, apoptosis, Fas signalling and activation-induced cell death determines which cells survive, while calcineurin signalling transmits TCR strength and thymocyte migration moves cells through the thymic niches. The cluster as a whole describes how the thymus generates a self-tolerant T cell repertoire.

theme: HDL assembly and ABCA1-mediated cholesterol efflux
story: The centre is reverse cholesterol transport initiated by ABCA1, which exports cellular cholesterol and phospholipid to apolipoprotein A-I to form nascent HDL; Tangier disease (defective ABCA1) shows its failure. Positive and negative regulation of cholesterol efflux, intracellular lipid transport, apoA-I signalling and HDL clearance describe control points, and cellular response to cholesterol and sterol homeostasis are the purpose they serve. The cluster is about removing excess cholesterol from peripheral cells via HDL.

theme: Non-vesicular lipid transfer between organelle membranes
story: The centre is protein-mediated lipid transfer between membranes, such as PI/PC exchange between ER and Golgi and transfer of phospholipids to membranes. Glycosphingolipid, glycolipid and ceramide-1-phosphate transport extend the same mechanism to sphingolipids, and PI synthesis supplies a key transferred lipid. The cluster describes how lipids made in the ER are delivered to other organelles without vesicles.

theme: Extracellular matrix and basement membrane assembly and adhesion
story: The centre is construction of the extracellular matrix: collagen synthesis, trimerisation, crosslinking and fibril organisation, elastic fibres, proteoglycans and basement membrane assembly with laminins. Integrin interactions, hemidesmosomes, anchoring fibrils and collagen-activated receptor signalling connect cells to this matrix. The cluster as a whole describes building the structural scaffold of tissues and attaching cells to it.

theme: Regulation of oxidative and hypoxic stress-induced cell death
story: The centre is the intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptotic pathway triggered by oxidative stress and hydrogen peroxide, with mitochondrial depolarisation as a key step. Responses to hypoxia and oxygen-glucose deprivation are related ischaemic stresses that feed into the same pathway, and paired positive and negative regulators determine whether cells survive or die. The cluster describes how cells decide between tolerating and dying from oxidative and ischaemic injury.

theme: Mammary gland epithelial lineage development and lactation
story: The centre is the mammary epithelial lineage hierarchy, from mammary stem cells to luminal, myoepithelial and alveolar cells. Epithelial proliferation, differentiation and alveolus development describe gland maturation during pregnancy. Lactation is the functional endpoint; the cluster is about building milk-producing mammary tissue.

theme: Centrosome microtubule organisation and mitotic spindle positioning
story: The centre is the centrosome as microtubule-organising centre: microtubule nucleation and anchoring, recruitment of centrosomal proteins and NuMA, Aurora A activation by TPX2, and centriole cohesion. Astral microtubules, cortical protein localisation and spindle orientation explain how the spindle is positioned in the cell, which governs asymmetric cell division. The cluster is about building and placing the mitotic spindle via centrosome-driven microtubule arrays.

theme: mRNA 3' end formation and decay
story: The centre is mRNA 3' end processing: co-transcriptional cleavage and polyadenylation, including for intronless pre-mRNAs. Decapping and 5'-to-3' exonucleolytic decay, plus deadenylation-independent decay, describe the opposite end of the mRNA life cycle. The cluster as a whole covers the birth and death of the mRNA tail and cap that set transcript stability.

theme: Erythrocyte gas exchange and Rh-mediated ammonium transport
story: The centre is red cell gas transport: haemoglobin oxygen loading/unloading, carbonic anhydrase hydration of CO2 and CO2 transmembrane transport. Rhesus glycoproteins (RHAG and Rh blood group) transport ammonium, linking to ammonium homeostasis and transepithelial transport, while basigin with MCT1 moves lactate and protons. The cluster describes membrane transport of small metabolic gases and waste molecules, centred on the erythrocyte membrane.

theme: Embryonic heart morphogenesis and cardiac lineage specification
story: The centre is heart development: cardiac progenitor specification and myoblast differentiation, heart tube formation and left-right looping, and chamber and septum formation. Secondary heart field contributions, cardiac neural crest migration and pharyngeal arch artery remodelling build the outflow tract and great arteries, while conduction system development (sinoatrial node, atrioventricular node, His-Purkinje) and coronary arteries complete the organ. Transcription factor networks such as TFAP2 underpin these lineages; the cluster describes building the four-chambered heart.

theme: p53 stability and activity control after DNA damage
story: The centre is regulation of TP53 by phosphorylation and ubiquitin-mediated degradation, with COP1 autodegradation removing a p53 E3 ligase. Serine/threonine phosphorylation and dephosphorylation terms reflect the kinase-phosphatase switches (e.g., ATM/CHK and PPM1D) that stabilise or release p53. Cdc25A degradation and p53 activation of DNA repair genes are parallel outputs of the same checkpoint; the cluster is about how DNA damage stabilises p53 and arrests the cell cycle.

theme: Base excision repair of damaged DNA bases
story: The centre is base excision repair: DNA glycosylases (OGG1, MUTYH, NTHL1, NEIL1, NEIL3) recognise and cleave damaged purines and pyrimidines, APEX1 displaces them and incises the AP site, and POLB and PCNA-dependent pathways fill the gap via short- or long-patch repair. The many 'defective' entries describe cancer-predisposing glycosylase variants that fail at substrate binding, processing or localisation. NEIL3-mediated interstrand cross-link resolution shows an extended use; the cluster is about removing oxidised and otherwise damaged bases from DNA.

theme: Thyroid hormone synthesis and sulfonation (PAPS) metabolism
story: The centre is thyroid hormone production: iodide uptake by NIS (SLC5A5), hydrogen peroxide generation for iodination, thyroid hormone transport and activity regulation. A second arm is cytosolic sulfonation using PAPS, whose synthesis and transport (PAPSS2 defects causing skeletal dysplasia) also inactivate thyroid hormones, along with selenium metabolism that supplies selenoprotein deiodinases. The cluster as a whole concerns thyroid hormone generation and the conjugation and trace-element pathways that tune its activity.

theme: Glutamate-glutamine nitrogen metabolism and carboxylate transport
story: The centre is glutamate and glutamine metabolism, which carry and release nitrogen, linking to ammonium homeostasis and nitrogen utilisation. The malate-aspartate shuttle and aspartate/asparagine metabolism connect these amino acids to mitochondrial redox and the TCA cycle, while sodium-coupled di- and tricarboxylate transporters (succinate, citrate) and SLC17A5 (Salla disease) move the associated organic anions across membranes. The cluster describes how amino acid nitrogen and TCA intermediates are exchanged between compartments.

theme: MECP2 chromatin regulation of neuronal gene expression
story: The centre is MECP2, which binds methylated (5mC and 5hmC) DNA and recruits NCoR/SMRT-HDAC complexes to regulate neuronal genes, including receptors, channels, ligands and GABA signalling components; Rett syndrome loss-of-function variants define the disease arm. The untitled module on neuronal RNA-binding proteins (ELAVL3, CPEB3, YBX1) and translational repression adds post-transcriptional control in neurons. Sensory and behavioural terms (touch, proprioception, visual behaviour) reflect neurological functions disrupted when MECP2 fails; the cluster is about epigenetic and translational control of neuronal function.

theme: APOBEC3 cytidine deamination restricting retroviruses
story: The centre is APOBEC3G-mediated restriction of HIV-1: cytidine deamination of viral DNA during reverse transcription, which HIV counters by Vif-mediated APOBEC3G degradation. Retroviral life cycle steps (integration, 2-LTR circle formation, translational frameshifting) and host suppression of viral replication and transcription show the targets of this defence, and cytidine-to-uridine RNA editing and the editosome reflect the related APOBEC1 activity. The cluster is about nucleic-acid editing enzymes as an intrinsic antiviral defence.

theme: Integrated stress response and unfolded protein response
story: The centre is the integrated stress response, in which eIF2alpha kinases (GCN2 for amino acid starvation, HRI for heme deficiency and mitochondrial stress, PERK for ER stress) repress global translation initiation while allowing selective translation. The ER unfolded protein response (PERK and IRE1 branches), mitochondrial UPR and UFMylation, which participates in ER homeostasis, are the stress sources and parallel adaptive arms. The cluster as a whole describes how cells sense protein-folding and nutrient stress and remodel translation to cope.

theme: MicroRNA and siRNA biogenesis and RNA silencing
story: The centre is small RNA biogenesis (miRNA and siRNA processing, RISC assembly) and the post-transcriptional silencing it drives through translational repression and mRNA destabilisation. Specific targets (CDH1, CDH11, PD-L1, NPAS4, PTEN via competing endogenous RNAs) show silencing in action, and miRNA decay and lncRNA sponging represent regulation of the regulators. P-body assembly and small-RNA-guided transcriptional regulation extend the theme; the cluster describes gene silencing by small RNAs.

theme: Mitochondrial respiratory chain complex assembly
story: The centre is assembly of the oxidative phosphorylation complexes, specifically complex I (NADH dehydrogenase), complex III and ATP synthase. Protein insertion into the mitochondrial inner membrane from the matrix provides the membrane subunits these complexes need. The cluster as a whole is about building the mitochondrial respiratory machinery that produces ATP.

theme: Oncogene-induced senescence and senescence-associated heterochromatin
story: The centre is cellular senescence, especially oncogene-induced senescence as a tumour-suppressive barrier. Formation of senescence-associated heterochromatin foci and subtelomeric heterochromatin represent the chromatin remodelling that locks proliferation genes off, and blocking the G0-to-G1 transition expresses the permanent arrest. Positive and negative regulation of senescence frame the decision; the cluster is about the stable arrest programme triggered by oncogenic stress.

theme: Vascular smooth muscle tone and blood pressure regulation
story: The centre is the contraction and relaxation of vascular smooth muscle, balanced between vasoconstrictors (endothelin, catecholamines) and vasodilators acting through NO and cGMP (eNOS trafficking, cGMP synthesis and effects, guanylyl cyclase signalling). Renal sodium excretion and urine volume (natriuretic peptide-cGMP signalling) add the volume arm, and systemic and pulmonary pressure regulation are the outcomes. The cluster describes how arterial tone and blood pressure are controlled.

theme: Excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic assembly via neurexin-neuroligin
story: The centre is synapse organisation driven by neurexin-neuroligin adhesion, which clusters PSD-95 and NMDA receptors at excitatory synapses and gephyrin and GABA-A receptors at inhibitory synapses. Presynaptic vesicle clustering and terminal bouton organisation are the matching presynaptic side. Regulation of excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic potentials and glutamatergic and GABAergic transmission are the functional outputs; the cluster is about assembling synapses and setting their excitation-inhibition balance.

theme: Nuclear RNA processing: splicing, 3' end formation and surveillance
story: The centre is pre-mRNA splicing: snRNA transcription, snRNP and tri-snRNP assembly, spliceosome formation and catalytic rearrangements, major and minor pathways and splice-site recognition. 3' end processing (polyadenylation, histone stem-loop processing, Pol II and Pol III termination) and nuclear RNA surveillance and decay by the exosome (CUTs, snRNA, rRNA, tRNA) are the companion maturation and quality control steps, also covering snRNA, snoRNA and rRNA processing. The cluster as a whole describes how the nucleus produces mature, quality-checked RNAs.

theme: Telomere maintenance by telomerase, capping and ALT suppression
story: The centre is telomere length maintenance by telomerase: holoenzyme assembly, telomerase RNA localisation via Cajal bodies (scaRNA, RNA folding) and extension of telomere ends. Telomere capping, packaging and protection from NHEJ prevent chromosome ends from being treated as breaks, while DAXX/ATRX-dependent inhibition of recombination suppresses the alternative lengthening of telomeres pathway. Subtelomeric heterochromatin and senescence regulation reflect the consequences; the cluster is about keeping chromosome ends intact and long enough for continued division.

theme: Myeloid and granulocyte lineage differentiation
story: The centre is transcriptional control of granulopoiesis, with RUNX1, PU.1 and retinoic acid receptor programmes committing haematopoietic and myeloid progenitors to neutrophil, eosinophil and mast cell fates. G-CSF and GM-CSF signalling drive expansion and maturation of these lineages, and the CSF/retinoid/WNT receptor network ties cytokine and retinoid inputs to the same programme. The cluster as a whole describes how bone marrow produces granulocytes.
